raw_response:
I have 10.1 mu of land, all in wheat-maize rotation. I have been doing this for 15 years and I know what works on my field. I am not going to change much this year because last year was decent and change is risky.

For wheat, I plant in mid-October. Last year I used Luyuan 502, but this year the seed dealer is pushing Jimai 22 and my cousin two villages over got about 550 kg per mu with it. So I will buy Jimai 22. I need 25 jin of seed per mu, which means about 250 jin total for my 10.1 mu. I pay about 3.5 yuan per jin, so that is about 875 yuan for wheat seed. I spread it with a machine after rotary tilling the field. Rotary tillage is what everyone does here — the soil is too compacted if you don't.

For wheat fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at planting. I buy the 15-15-15 bag, about 80 jin per mu. For 10 mu that is 800 jin, so I buy 8 bags of 100 jin each. Each bag costs about 180 yuan, so that is 1,440 yuan. Then in late March when the wheat is at jointing stage, I topdress with urea. I put about 50 jin of urea per mu — that is 500 jin total, 5 bags at 130 yuan each, so 650 yuan. I learned from the input dealer that jointing is when wheat needs nitrogen the most. Some years I put a bit more if the wheat looks yellow, because losing yield is worse than wasting a little fertilizer.

I irrigate wheat three times. First is the winter irrigation around the New Year to protect from freezing. Then in spring I water twice — once at jointing and once at grain filling. Each time the pump runs for about 3 hours and burns 8 liters of diesel, so each irrigation costs me about 50 yuan in fuel. Three times for wheat is 150 yuan. I have a well, so I do not pay for water, but the pump maintenance costs money too.

For wheat pests, I spray herbicide once in March when the weeds come up. That costs about 80 yuan for the chemical for my whole field. I spray insecticide once for aphids, about 60 yuan. If the spring is rainy and humid, I also spray fungicide once, which is another 70 yuan. Last year I did the fungicide spray and it paid off. This year the weather looks normal but I will probably do it anyway — it is cheap insurance.

For maize, I plant Denghai 605 right after wheat harvest in early June. Everyone around here uses Denghai 605 — it is a hybrid seed and it yields good if you water it. I buy 2 kg of seed per mu, so 20 kg total. The dealer charges 50 yuan per kg for this hybrid, so that is 1,000 yuan. I plant no-tillage directly into the wheat stubble with a precision planter. No-tillage saves me time and diesel, and by June I am in a hurry to get the maize in before the rains stop.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer at planting — about 60 jin per mu, so 600 jin total, 6 bags, about 1,080 yuan. Then when the maize is knee-high, I side-dress urea, about 50 jin per mu, so another 500 jin, 5 bags, 650 yuan. Some farmers put everything at once but I side-dress because the dealer told me the maize takes up nitrogen mostly during the fast-growing period.

Irrigation for maize depends on the summer rain. Last two years July was dry so I irrigated twice — once at the seven-leaf stage and once at tasseling. I will plan for two times again. If it rains a lot I might skip one, but I would rather have the water ready. Two irrigations at 50 yuan each is 100 yuan.

For maize pests, I spray herbicide once right after planting — pre-emergence — that is about 90 yuan for the field. Then I spray insecticide once for corn borers, about 70 yuan. The seed comes treated now so sometimes the insecticide is enough with just one spray.

I think about my whole budget. Seeds cost me about 1,875 yuan for the year. Fertilizer is the biggest expense — about 3,820 yuan. Pesticides are maybe 370 yuan. Irrigation diesel is about 250 yuan. For harvest I hire a combine — 100 yuan per mu for wheat and 90 yuan per mu for maize, so about 1,919 yuan total. My wife and I do most of the planting and spraying ourselves, but at harvest time I hire one laborer for a day to help move bags, which is 150 yuan per day.

I expect about 520 kg per mu for wheat and 600 kg per mu for maize. Wheat is about 2.4 yuan per kg and maize is about 2.2 yuan per kg these days. If I hit those yields, that covers all my costs and leaves some money for my kid's school and for next year's inputs. But if the weather turns bad or prices drop, I still need to eat, so I make sure I put enough fertilizer down — a bad harvest is a disaster I cannot afford.
